name: sortable-list

frames.best_why: All five rows are stacked in order with checkbox, number and label clearly readable.

tagline: Checkbox task rows you drag up or down to reorder.
summary: A stacked task list where each row has a checkbox, a number and a label; rows can be dragged to reorder, and checking one shrinks it and reveals a delete button.
appearance: Five dark rounded rows stack with small gaps on black. Each row holds a round outline checkbox, a faint order number and light grey text; a checked row narrows and shows a red trash icon.
behaviour: Dragging a row lifts it while the others spring aside; checking the box turns the label red, then shrinks the row and slides a delete button in from the side.
demo_content: Tasks Design system tokens, Component architecture, Write unit tests, Review pull request and Update documentation.
search_phrases: todo list with checkboxes and delete
task list that animates when reordered
reorderable list for a project board
todo items that collapse when done
list rows that spring into place
use_when: Users need to set the order of a short task or playlist list themselves, not just tick items off.
avoid_when: The list is long; dragging every row is slow and there is no search or keyboard reorder.
customise: items and setItems drive the rows while renderItem controls each row's markup; drag, collapse and delete animations are fixed in the source.
weight_why: A handful of rows with layout springs that run only while dragging or toggling.

a11y.note: Reordering is pointer-only; checkboxes work from the keyboard but their label says Mark to delete for a completion action.

issues: Rows can only be reordered with a pointer; there is no keyboard path.
A checked row replaces its title with the word Delete, so done tasks lose their name.
The checkbox aria-label says Mark to delete although it marks completion.
polish_why: Springy reorder and a neat collapse; done rows swapping their label for Delete is odd.
